extracted.intended_audience: small business SBIR/STTR applicants and institutional/subaward grant administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing an SBIR/STTR application including the required budget (Sections A–K), budget justification, subaward details, SBIR/STTR eligibility questions, and a Phase II commercialization plan (executive summary, value/outcomes/impact, company, leadership, funding history, business/regulatory/reimbursement strategy, market/customer/competition analysis).

rubrics_metrics.name: RESEARCH & RELATED Budget Sections A–K
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget must be organized into Sections A through K (Section A: Senior/Key Person; B: Other Personnel; C: Equipment; D: Travel; E: Participant/Trainee Support Costs; F: Other Direct Costs; G: Direct Costs (A thru F); H: Indirect Costs; I: Total Direct and Indirect Costs; J: Fee; K: Budget Justification attachment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each section should supply Funds Requested ($) and subtotal/totals (e.g., Total Direct Costs (A thru F), Total Indirect Costs). Attach only one Budget Justification file (filename and MIME type).

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior/Key Person budget entries
rubrics_metrics.description: For each senior/key person include Prefix, First/Middle/Last Name, Project Role, Base Salary ($), Calendar Months, Academic Months, Sum Months, Requested Salary ($), Fringe Benefits ($), and Funds Requested ($).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List all senior/key personnel and provide totals. Example entries shown (e.g., Constance Benson, M.D. Consortium PI 0.60 cal months). Provide a narrative justification of roles and percent effort in the budget justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Personnel budget entries
rubrics_metrics.description: List other personnel by number and role (postdoctoral associates, graduate students, undergraduate students, secretarial/clerical), calendar/academic/sum months, requested salary, fringe, and Funds Requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide totals for number of personnel and total salary, wages and fringe benefits (A + B). Include named staff in justification (e.g., study coordinator, regulatory specialist) and their calendar-month effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment listing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe and list items and dollar amount for each equipment item exceeding $5,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide equipment item name and Funds Requested ($) and include a Total funds requested for all equipment listed and an attached file if additional equipment is itemized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel cost categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget separately for Domestic Travel Costs (including Canada, Mexico, and U.S. possessions) and Foreign Travel Costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide Funds Requested ($) for each travel category and include justification in the budget narrative as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant/trainee support costs
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicable, provide Participant/Trainee Support Costs broken out into Tuition/Fees/Health Insurance, Stipends, Travel, Subsistence, Other, and Number of Participants/Trainees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide totals for participant/trainee support and justify in attached documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Direct Costs categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Other Direct Costs (Section F) must include items such as Materials and Supplies, Publication Costs, Consultant Services, ADP/Computer Services, Subawards/Consortium/Contractual Costs, Equipment or Facility Rental/User Fees, Alterations and Renovations, Communications and Computing, Outpatient Care Costs, and other specified line items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Itemize and justify each Other Direct Cost in the Budget Justification (e.g., supplies for laboratory disposables, patient care costs for testing 200 samples, communications costs tied to project personnel).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect costs entry format
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify Indirect Cost Type, Indirect Cost Rate (%), Indirect Cost Base ($), and Funds Requested ($).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide cognizant federal agency contact info where applicable. Example given: MTDC, On Campus Rate 55.00% with DHHS Region IX as cognizant agency. Show calculations and base for the applied rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Totals and fee calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate Total Direct Costs (G), Total Indirect Costs (H), Total Direct and Indirect Costs (I = G + H), and any institutional costs or Fees (J).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure line-item subtotals roll up correctly and match the overall Funds Requested totals on the budget forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget Justification attachment and narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: Attach one Budget Justification file and provide narrative justification for personnel, supplies, patient care costs, communications/computing, and other line items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrative should describe each senior and key person's role, percent effort and responsibilities (e.g., recruitment, consent, specimen handling), justify supplies (e.g., gloves, blood collection materials), explain patient care testing costs (e.g., HIV EIA, NAT per-sample costs), and communications costs tied to project staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subaward/Consortium details
rubrics_metrics.description: For each subaward include Organizational DUNS, Budget Type (Project/Subaward/Consortium), name of organization, Start Date, End Date, and Budget Period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full subaward budgets and attach subaward-specific budget justifications/files. Include cumulative totals for subawards in the overall budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment dollar threshold rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Items exceeding $5,000 must be listed individually in the Equipment section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Smaller items may be included under Materials and Supplies; major equipment purchases require description and per-item dollar amounts and justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR applicant eligibility certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must certify that at time of award the organization meets the small business eligibility criteria defined in the FOA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond Yes/No and, if No, provide an explanation in an attached file. Eligibility applies to all SBIR/STTR applicants and is required for award processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of subcontracts with Federal laboratories or agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether the application includes subcontracts with Federal laboratories or other Federal Government agencies and insert the names if yes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full disclosure is required on the SBIR/STTR form when subcontracting involves federal entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic performance of R&D
rubrics_metrics.description: Certify whether all research and development on the project will be performed in its entirety in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not entirely in the U.S., provide an explanation in an attached file as required by the SBIR/STTR instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercialization Plan requirement (Phase II/Fast-Track)
rubrics_metrics.description: If submitting a Phase II or Phase I/Phase II Fast-Track application, include a Commercialization Plan in accordance with the agency announcement and/or agency-specific instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach the Commercialization Plan file. Questions 1–7 on the SBIR/STTR form must be completed by all applicants; the Commercialization Plan is required for Phase II and Fast-Track submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR personnel and employment questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide anticipated number of personnel to be employed at the organization at time of award and indicate whether the Project Director/PI will have primary employment with the small business at the time of award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer Yes/No as applicable and provide supporting attachments if required. This information is used to determine eligibility and project staffing.

rubrics_metrics.name: STTR-specific PI appointment and effort rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For STTR, indicate whether the Project Director/PI has a formal appointment/commitment with the small business or research institution AND will devote at least 10% effort to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions apply to STTR applications only; provide documentation of appointment/commitment and percent effort as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work-share percentages for STTR collaborations
rubrics_metrics.description: In joint R&D proposed in an STTR application, the small business must perform at least 40% of the work and the research institution at least 30% of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear statement of planned percent effort/work allocation between partners in the application materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercialization Plan structure and content expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: A comprehensive Commercialization Plan should include an Executive Summary; Value of the SBIR/STTR Project, Expected Outcomes, and Impact; Company description and Leadership; Funding History; Business Strategy; Regulatory Strategy; Reimbursement Strategy; and Market, Customer, and Competition analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete market sizing, expected outcomes, product applications, partnerships, timelines for regulatory approvals and commercialization, and specific commercialization activities (e.g., strategic partnerships, venture financing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory strategy and quality systems expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipate regulatory filings (e.g., CE Mark, US FDA 510(k) or PMA) and implement Quality Systems under 21 CFR 820 and ISO 13485, with Design Control and cGMP-compliant pilot production where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State regulatory pathway for each product (e.g., CD4 enumeration self-certified in Europe vs 510(k) in the US; HIV diagnostic may require PMA in US), timelines for filings, and plans for meeting regulatory standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reimbursement strategy expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on indications with established CPT codes and purchasing channels to reduce commercialization risk and consider opportunities such as code stacking (e.g., tests reporting both antibody and antigen).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain reimbursement landscape, CPT codes, likely payers/customers, and sales channels in the plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market analysis and metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide market estimates (global and segmented by region), projected units, percent share, average selling price (ASP), and market value projections (example table format for US/Europe vs Rest of World and future years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factor in demand drivers (screening initiatives, guidelines), procurement channels (WHO, Global Fund, PEPFAR), and clinical usage assumptions (e.g., CD4/viral load frequency). Include segmented product markets (clinical screening, antenatal screening, CD4, viral monitor, co-infection panels).

rubrics_metrics.name: WHO procurement suitability criteria (limited-resource settings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Products intended for limited-resource environments should operate on battery power, require no refrigeration, and be simple to operate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address these criteria explicitly when proposing products for WHO/NGO procurement and bulk purchasing schemes to increase adoption by global health purchasers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition and landscape analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify existing competitors by segment (e.g., Abbott Point of Care, HemoCue, Siemens; lateral flow manufacturers like Alere, Quidel, Becton Dickinson) and describe competitive positioning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss competitors’ strengths, product types, market share, and how the proposed product differentiates (e.g., multiplexing, sensitivity, portability, cost).

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding history and use of funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe prior funding sources (research grants/contracts, parent company support, private investment, product sales), amounts, and how those funds were used to advance development/commercialization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show how prior competitive awards and investments validate technology and provide runway for next milestones; include funding amounts, remaining contract balances, and product sales where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business strategy for product/portfolio development
rubrics_metrics.description: State a clear business strategy: focus internal resources on selected high-value applications, use partnerships or licensing for other applications, and target markets with unmet needs (e.g., infectious disease POC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe go-to-market approach, partner/licensee strategy, targeting of established reimbursement channels, and prioritization criteria for internal development versus external partnerships.
